name: Fix a selector that matches nothing
objective: CKAD core: label and annotate objects, and target them with equality + set-based selectors. Add/overwrite/remove labels, bulk-label via a selector, set-based matching, matchExpressions selectors, annotations, and a selector-mismatch diagnose-fix. Graded exactly.

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a selector that matches nothing
questions.teach:
A Service with **no endpoints** despite healthy pods means its selector doesn't match any pod labels. Compare `kubectl get svc <s> -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'` to `kubectl get pods --show-labels` and loosen/fix the selector.

**Gotcha:** removing a selector key via patch needs `key: null` (a plain merge keeps it).
questions.prompt:
Service `shop-svc` in `labels-learn` selects `app=shop,tier=cache` — but no pod has `tier=cache`, so it has zero endpoints. Fix the selector so it fronts the `app=shop` pods. Don't delete it.

Target: `shop-svc` has at least one endpoint.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n labels-learn get svc shop-svc -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'` shows `tier: cache`. Remove it: `kubectl -n labels-learn patch svc shop-svc -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"shop","tier":null}}}'`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n labels-learn patch svc shop-svc -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"shop","tier":null}}}'
kubectl -n labels-learn get endpoints shop-svc -o wide
questions.eli5:
Picture a mail-forwarding desk at an office. People send letters to **"shop-svc"**, and the desk is supposed to forward each letter to whichever desks (pods) match a description on a sticky note. Right now the sticky note says: *"forward to anyone wearing an `app=shop` badge **and** a `tier=cache` badge."*

Problem: nobody in the building wears a `tier=cache` badge. So the forwarding desk looks around, finds zero matching people, and every letter just piles up undelivered. In Kubernetes terms, the Service has **no endpoints** — even though healthy `app=shop` pods are sitting right there.

The fix is to loosen the description on the sticky note so it only asks for the badge people actually wear: just `app=shop`. Then the desk finds the pods and starts forwarding.

To check who's wearing what, you compare two things: what the note *asks for* (`kubectl get svc shop-svc -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'`) against what people *actually wear* (`kubectl get pods --show-labels`).

**Watch out:**

- **Healthy pods + zero endpoints = a selector mismatch**, almost every time. The pods aren't broken; the Service just can't find them.
- **Don't delete the Service** — just repair its selector. Deleting throws away the stable name and address other apps rely on.
- **To *remove* a selector key with `patch`, set it to `null`** (`"tier": null`). A plain merge patch only *adds or changes* keys — it will quietly keep the old `tier: cache` and your fix won't take.
- Selector keys are **AND-ed**: asking for `app=shop` **and** `tier=cache` means a pod must have *both*. One unmatched key is enough to match nothing.
- Give it a second after patching — endpoints repopulate almost instantly, but verify with `kubectl get endpoints shop-svc`.
questions.deepDive:
## Diagnose & fix a Service selector that matches nothing

### The one-sentence model
**A Service finds its pods by label selector; the endpoints controller lists every pod whose labels are a superset of `spec.selector`.** No pod matches → zero endpoints → traffic goes nowhere, even though the pods are perfectly healthy.

### How a Service finds pods
```
Service.spec.selector  ──(must ALL match, AND-ed)──▶  Pod.metadata.labels
         │
         ▼
   EndpointSlice / Endpoints  ◀── the controller fills this with matching Ready pod IPs
```
- A Service selector is **equality-only** and **AND-ed**: every `key: value` must be present on the pod.
- A pod may carry *extra* labels — only the keys in the selector matter.
- Only **Ready** pods (passing readiness) become endpoint addresses.

### Diagnosing
```bash
# 1. What does the Service ask for?
kubectl -n labels-learn get svc shop-svc -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'; echo
#   {"app":"shop","tier":"cache"}

# 2. What labels do the pods actually have?
kubectl -n labels-learn get pods --show-labels

# 3. Does the Service have any endpoints?
kubectl -n labels-learn get endpoints shop-svc
kubectl -n labels-learn get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=shop-svc
```
`ENDPOINTS` column shows `<none>` → the selector matches no pod. Compare the two and find the offending key (`tier: cache` here — no pod has it).

### Fixing — remove the bad selector key
A **strategic/merge patch adds or overwrites keys; it never deletes them.** To drop a key you must set it to `null`:
```bash
kubectl -n labels-learn patch svc shop-svc \
  -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"shop","tier":null}}}'
```
Result: selector becomes just `{"app":"shop"}`, which matches the pods.

### Ways to change a selector
| Method | Command | Removes a key? |
|---|---|---|
| Merge patch + `null` | `kubectl patch svc s -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"tier":null}}}'` | ✅ (that's the trick) |
| JSON patch `remove` | `kubectl patch svc s --type=json -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/selector/tier"}]'` | ✅ |
| `kubectl edit svc s` | hand-edit YAML, delete the line | ✅ |
| Plain merge patch | `kubectl patch svc s -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"shop"}}}'` | ❌ keeps `tier` |

> **Do not** `kubectl apply` a trimmed manifest expecting removal unless it was created with apply — and **don't delete/recreate** the Service when asked to fix it (loses the ClusterIP and name other clients depend on).

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Healthy pods but `<none>` endpoints ⇒ selector mismatch** almost always. Don't chase the pods — fix the Service.
- **Merge patch keeps old keys.** Removing a selector key needs `key: null` (or a JSON-patch `remove`). A plain merge quietly leaves `tier: cache` in place.
- Selector keys are **AND-ed** and **exact-match** — one unmatched key matches nothing.
- Endpoints only include **Ready** pods; a failing readiness probe also yields empty endpoints (different root cause, same symptom).
- **Keep the Service** — patch it, don't delete it.

### Quick reference
```bash
# diagnose
kubectl -n labels-learn get svc shop-svc -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'; echo
kubectl -n labels-learn get pods --show-labels
kubectl -n labels-learn get endpoints shop-svc

# fix (drop the tier key)
kubectl -n labels-learn patch svc shop-svc \
  -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"shop","tier":null}}}'

# verify
kubectl -n labels-learn get endpoints shop-svc -o wide   # now lists pod IPs
```
